extracted.intended_audience: recipients of Federal funding (educational institutions), Title IX coordinators, campus administrators, and legal counsel
extracted.subtask_description: Standards for recipient grievance procedures under Title IX, focusing on appeals and informal resolution (who may appeal, on what grounds, procedural protections, and limits on informal resolution). Intended to guide institutions in drafting and implementing compliant grievance and informal resolution processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Records retention and nondiscriminatory handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must be mindful of adhering to any retention requirements in State law and in their own policies. Recipients also must not treat or categorize records in a manner that results in discrimination based on sex under the Department's regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In other words, a recipient cannot treat people differently on the basis of their sex with respect to records pertaining to sexual harassment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equitable response for respondent prior to sanctions
rubrics_metrics.description: An equitable response for a respondent means a grievance process that complies with §106.45 before the imposition of any disciplinary sanctions or other actions that are not supportive measures, as defined in §106.30.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutions should not impose non-supportive disciplinary actions on a respondent until the §106.45 grievance process has been followed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equal appeal rights to both parties
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must offer both parties equal appeal rights on determinations regarding responsibility and dismissals of formal complaints (or allegations therein).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complainants and respondents have equal appeal rights under the final regulations; limitations that prevented complainants from appealing sanctions were removed. Equal appeals increase legitimacy and allow self-correction of erroneous outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required bases for appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must offer appeals on at least the following three bases: (1) procedural irregularity that affected the outcome; (2) new evidence that was not reasonably available when the determination was made that could affect the outcome; or (3) the Title IX Coordinator, investigator, or decision-maker had a general or specific conflict of interest or bias against the complainant or respondent that affected the outcome.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients may offer appeals on additional bases, but any additional bases must be offered equally to both parties. These specified bases narrow what qualifies as a justifiable appeal and focus on errors affecting accuracy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to appeal dismissals
rubrics_metrics.description: Both parties may appeal a recipient's dismissal of a formal complaint (or allegations therein), whether the dismissal was mandatory or discretionary under §106.45(b)(3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appeals allow correction where a dismissal was based on incorrect facts or erroneous application of jurisdictional criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeals on severity of sanctions discretionary but must be equal
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether parties can appeal based solely on the severity of sanctions is left to the recipient's discretion; if a recipient allows appeals on that basis, both parties must have equal opportunity to appeal on that basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The NPRM limitation precluding complainants from appealing severity was removed; recipients decide whether to include sanction-proportionality as an appeal ground but must apply it equally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal decision-maker independence
rubrics_metrics.description: Appeal decision-makers must be different individuals than the Title IX Coordinator, any investigator, or the decision-maker(s) that reached the initial determination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This separation ensures independent review; §106.45(b)(8)(iii) makes it clear the appeal decision-maker cannot be the same person as prior actors in the case.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal decision-maker anti-bias and training requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Appeal decision-makers must satisfy the robust anti-bias and training requirements of §106.45(b)(1)(iii).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appeal decision-makers must be free from bias and conflicts of interest and trained to serve impartially, which helps ensure fairness and reliability of appeal outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equal opportunity to submit written statements on appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: Both parties must be given a meaningful and equal opportunity to submit written statements supporting or challenging the outcome on appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appeals are not one-sided; the process must allow both complainant and respondent to present arguments in writing to the appeal reviewer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written determinations of appeal results
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must provide written determinations explaining the appeal result and rationales to both parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reasoned written decisions describing the appeal results should be given to both parties to increase transparency and legitimacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prompt time frames for appeals
rubrics_metrics.description: The appeal process must be concluded under designated, reasonably prompt time frames (see §106.45(b)(1)(v)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prompt resolution of appeals reduces burdens on parties and helps ensure that final determinations are both accurate and timely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipients may offer additional appeal bases equally
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients may offer appeals on additional grounds beyond the three required bases, but such additional bases for appeal must be offered equally to both parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flexibility is permitted so long as parity between complainant and respondent is maintained.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeals help ensure accurate, fair outcomes for high-stakes interests
rubrics_metrics.description: Appeal rights exist because complainants and respondents have different but significant life-altering interests; appeals provide a mechanism to correct errors and increase confidence in outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department emphasizes appeals' role in correcting procedural irregularity, bias, or newly discovered evidence, and in reducing reliance on external litigation or OCR enforcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipients' discretion balanced with mandatory equal-protection requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: While recipients retain flexibility and discretion to craft Title IX grievance procedures tailored to their communities, they must comply with mandatory requirements such as offering equal appeals and meeting anti-bias and training standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients are in the best position to design procedures but must implement the core protections required by the regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Informal resolution available but not default
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients may offer an informal resolution process to resolve a formal complaint without completing the investigation and adjudication, but informal resolution is not the default and may only be offered after a formal complaint is filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department declines to make informal resolution mandatory or a prerequisite to formal process; voluntary participation is required and formal complaint must exist before informal resolution is offered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voluntariness and non-waiver of formal process in informal resolution
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients are explicitly prohibited from requiring students or employees to waive their right to a formal §106.45 grievance process as a condition of enrollment or employment or enjoyment of any other right; recipients are explicitly prohibited from requiring parties to participate in informal resolution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participation in informal resolution must be voluntary, and parties retain the right to pursue formal grievance procedures instead.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to withdraw from informal resolution
rubrics_metrics.description: Either party has the right to withdraw from informal resolution and resume a §106.45 grievance process at any time before agreeing to a resolution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This protection preserves party autonomy and prevents coercion into settlements before mutual agreement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits on use of informal resolution where employee alleged to have harassed student
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients are categorically prohibited from offering or facilitating an informal resolution process to resolve allegations that an employee sexually harassed a student.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Due to power differentials and potential undue influence, informal resolution cannot be used in employee-on-student sexual harassment formal complaints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Informal resolution facilitator standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Individuals facilitating informal resolution must be free from conflicts of interest, bias, and trained to serve impartially.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Facilitators should have appropriate training and neutrality similar to formal process actors; the Department revised §106.45(b)(9) to require these qualities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Informal resolution procedural transparency and notice requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The initial written notice of allegations sent to both parties must include information about any informal resolution processes the recipient has chosen to make available and must disclose any consequences resulting from participating in informal resolution, including records that will be maintained or could be shared.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients should clearly inform parties about informal options and potential consequences (e.g., records retention, use of facilitators as witnesses) before parties consent to mediation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Informal resolution time frames
rubrics_metrics.description: Informal resolution processes must have reasonably prompt time frames.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely completion of informal resolution helps protect parties' interests and ensures the process does not unduly delay access to remedies or formal adjudication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure regarding informal resolution facilitators as witnesses
rubrics_metrics.description: The recipient may allow informal resolution facilitators to serve as witnesses in subsequent formal grievance processes, but if recipients would accept such witnesses, that possibility must be clearly disclosed to the parties as part of the written notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transparency about potential consequences of participating in informal resolution (including witness status) is required so parties can make informed, voluntary choices.
